# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need the manual’s exact rule before choosing a wire. I’m asking Mute to provide it and to help establish a reliable gesture protocol with Deaf; my gesture alone cannot carry arbitrary meanings to Deaf yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send me the manual's complete rule and tell me exactly what visual facts Deaf must report. Also establish with Deaf a protocol for reporting wire positions and markings using gestures.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The bomb display reads 8. The light is green. The wires, in order, are wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, and wire 3 blue.

I know the physical facts now: display 8, green light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I still do not know which condition the manual assigns to which wire, so cutting now would be unsafe. I’m sending these facts to Mute and requesting the exact rule.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have received: display 8, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. What does the manual say to cut for this combination?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's gesture messages, in order: one: thumbs up, OK hand, raised open palm, love-you hand, clapping hands. Two: four pointing-up hands, thumbs up, raised open palm, love-you hand, handshake. Three: seven pointing-up hands, love-you hand, thumbs up, raised open palm, handshake. Four: eight pointing-up hands, raised open palm, love-you hand, thumbs up, clapping hands. Five: eight pointing-up hands, OK hand, love-you hand, raised open palm, thumbs up.

The five gesture reports are not self-interpreting to me: Deaf can identify their shapes, but no meaning has been established for those signs. They appear to encode manual information, so I must have Mute decode them rather than guess a wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf relayed five gesture sequences: (1) one pointing-up hand, thumbs up, OK hand, raised open palm, love-you hand, clapping hands; (2) four pointing-up hands, thumbs up, raised open palm, love-you hand, handshake; (3) seven pointing-up hands, love-you hand, thumbs up, raised open palm, handshake; (4) eight pointing-up hands, raised open palm, love-you hand, thumbs up, clapping hands; (5) eight pointing-up hands, OK hand, love-you hand, raised open palm, thumbs up. Please translate these into the manual's exact rule and tell me which wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New mute gesture message: pointing-up hand, then love-you hand.

Mute’s new two-sign message still has no established meaning for me, and the earlier sequences have not yielded an unambiguous rule. Since Mute can hear me, I’m requesting the decisive information in speech rather than asking Deaf to relay another opaque gesture code. I will not cut a wire without it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer in plain speech: for display 8, green light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, which exact wire position must I cut? If you cannot state it directly, explain the gesture code first.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New mute gesture message: eight pointing-up hands, OK hand, love-you hand, clapping hands, pointing-up hand, love-you hand.

Mute cannot answer in speech, so the gesture reports are the only available route. I can establish a simple response code in words that Mute understands: one gesture for each wire. I’m asking Mute to ignore the opaque multi-gesture encoding and return only the required wire number; Deaf can then identify that single gesture and report it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer the bomb decision directly with exactly one gesture: thumbs up means cut wire 1, victory hand means cut wire 2, love-you hand means cut wire 3. Do not send the longer encoded message.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute repeats: pointing-up hand, then love-you hand.

The two gestures do not follow the one-gesture protocol I requested, so I cannot safely infer a wire from them. I’m correcting the protocol explicitly: Mute must send exactly one gesture, with no preliminary sign; Deaf should report that single sign. Until then I will not act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your last message had two gestures and is ambiguous. Send exactly one gesture only: thumbs up means wire 1, victory hand means wire 2, love-you hand means wire 3. No other gesture or sequence.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture is one thumbs-up hand.

Mute’s single thumbs-up matches the protocol we established: thumbs up means cut wire 1. The known bomb facts are display 8, green light, and wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. I will now cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
